chunks: From him, from Fadala ibn Yasar, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Complete the rows when you find a gap, and it does not harm you if you lag behind when you find tightness in the row, and walk at an angle until you complete the row."

key_terms.خَلَلًا: Gap or vacancy in the row
key_terms.ضِيقًا: Tightness or crowding in the row

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on filling gaps in prayer rows and adjusting position if the row is crowded?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the communal discipline and visual perfection of the prayer row (saff), a key element of congregational worship in Shia jurisprudence. It balances the obligation of filling gaps with the practical flexibility of adjusting one's stance in crowded spaces, ensuring that the unity of the congregation is maintained without causing undue hardship. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic principle of facilitating collective worship while preserving its structural integrity.
